text:
sara: heads up — during the 11:40-11:45 peak batching window in us-west-2 we saw p95 east-west jump from ~8ms to ~120ms across several GPU racks, and a few worker pods reported lost RDMA streams. stack traces + short logs below. asking for quick triage :eyes:

mike: seeing same on the dashboard, spike aligns with our daily batch ramp. queues backed up and autoscaler spun up extra Dedicated pools. can we get NIC counters and rdma device stats?

chen: grabbing counters now. running: `ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "tx_|rx_|rx_nohandler"` and `ibv_devinfo -v`

chen: ethtool shows rising tx_errors on mlx5p2 intermittently. ibv_devinfo returns all ports up but psm2 logs show: `psm2: sendq stall, timeout` and some `ib_comp: queue pair flush due to error` lines.

julia: any recent config changes? mtu, qps, or iptables?

sara: we rolled an ingress firewall rule last night but only to controlplane subnets — shouldn't affect east-west. MTU pinned at 9000 on all nodes, no known LB changes.

nadeem: can we capture a short pcap on a couple of affected nodes for the next window? `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/ew-spike.pcap -c 20000` and also `rdma-sampler` on the same interval.

ops-bot: scheduled capture window 11:40-11:50 UTC, nodes: gnode-12,g-13,g-14.

mike: while we wait, try toggling GRO/GSO off on one node to see if it stabilizes: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` — that reduced similar symptoms in another cluster for us before.

chen: toggled on gnode-12 at 11:42. immediate improvement in p95 (120ms -> 22ms) for that node, others still noisy.

julia: interesting. suggests offload/path coalescing issue. can you check kernel dmesg for mlx5 messages?

chen: dmesg snippet:
```
[Mar 12 11:41:58] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: Unhandled PARST error, type 0x4
[Mar 12 11:41:59] psm2  : TX error on qp 1245, compl status 0x10
[Mar 12 11:42:01] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: FW fatal err (0x2)
```

nadeem: FW fatal err — could be NIC firmware acting up under high coalesced loads. Which firmware version? `ethtool -i eth0`.

chen: fw version 23.34.0 for the mlx5 family. I see a vendor patch rolled two months ago cluster-wide.

sara: recall a vendor advisory about a regression with large GSO + RDMA offloads. Does disabling GSO cluster-wide sound safe as a short mitigation? Impact: small CPU increase and potential higher cost if throughput drops.

mike: short mitigation +1. But let's scope: only apply to batching racks during peak windows via a DaemonSet toggle, not cluster-wide. Ops runbook step: annotate node `redwood/ew-gso-disable=true` and job runner picks it up.

julia: also check PMTU/ICMP filtering — if ICMP unreachable is blocked, PMTU discovery can fail and cause fragmentation/rertrans that surface as RDMA stalls. `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc`?

chen: pmTU looks fine (0). But I did find intermittent ICMP Destination Unreachable being dropped at our egress firewall for certain source CIDRs in the nodepool.

nadeem: that could explain path MTU mismatches under heavy batching when packets exceed negotiated size and are silently dropped. Let's open a firewall exception for intra-cluster ICMP temporarily.

deploy-bot: firewall rule rollback window scheduled at 11:50. Change request CR-5247.

mike: rolling exception now for farm-subnet 10.200.0.0/16 -> 10.200.0.0/16 ICMP allow, applied to cluster route table at 11:46.

chen: after rule change + GSO off on gnode-12/13, observed p95 back to ~10-25ms across sample nodes. RDMA sendq errors decreased in logs.

sara: good. action items:
- short: DaemonSet to disable GRO/GSO on batch racks during peak windows (mike)
- short: temporary ICMP allow for intra-cluster PMTU (nadeem) — revert after thorough validation
- medium: vendor engagement on firmware regression for mlx5 23.34.0 (julia)
- medium: add RDMA/psm2 metric alerts for TX error rate + queue stalls (chen)
- long: test a firmware upgrade path or hardware swap for persistent offenders (infra).

mike: will create the DaemonSet patch and a canary rollout to 3 nodes first. estimate 30m to PR and 1hr for rollout + observation.

julia: I'll ping vendor and share logs/pcap. also queue a maintenance window if vendor suggests FW rollback.

nadeem: ops will keep the firewall exception and monitor for side effects; revert in 6 hours unless signaled.

sara: thanks team — impact: some jobs got retried and Dedicated usage increased, expect a ~12% bump on today's infra spend attributed to autoscaler spur. i'll file cost note separately. closing slack thread once vendor confirms next steps. :white_check_mark:
